experiments.scope: Reduced event on the selected Orchard Poseidon target at its own round count: the first 14 bits of the big-endian reading of the 32-byte digest agree for two distinct canonical messages. One birthday search per organizer trial over fresh inputs from the trial seed. No full collision is expected or claimed.
experiments.hypothesis: A search of at most 1200 fresh inputs returns a pair whose digests agree on those 14 bits in every trial. The count of trials that return a pair is a reproducible observation; no probability, rate or population bound is drawn from it (public organizer seeds; nothing is assumed about the seeded trials being independent or identically distributed). Checks the digest of the selected target at one reduced width; it says nothing about the full-width map, the cost or the success probability.

experiments.scope: Euclidean normality of the algorithm's own construction at reduced depth, on the selected Orchard Poseidon target (proof.md 9.5, 10.5.1). For two centres c per trial (the first from the trial seed, the second from the seed and its index) the program builds F_2(c + X), the coordinate 0 after the first 2 S-box layers on the line j = 0 of the first two rounds (the F_N of proof.md 10.3, degree 25), its monic odd part g about c (degree m = 12), R = X^((p-1)/2) mod g and the complete Euclidean remainder sequence of (g, R - 1), exactly over F_p. Trials 0-255 are computed, 512 sequences (seed set a, entry 1 of 2). A trial whose two sequences are both normal (deg(R - 1) = m - 1 and every quotient of degree 1 down to the gcd) returns two distinct canonical messages on the line whose digests agree on the first 6 bits, found among 65 line points (certain, by pigeonhole); any other trial returns two nulls. No full collision is expected or claimed.
experiments.hypothesis: Every computed sequence is normal, so exactly 256 of the 256 trials return a pair. The count is a reproducible observation consistent with H-NORMAL; no bound on the abnormality rate is drawn from it (public organizer seeds; nothing is assumed about the seeded trials being independent or identically distributed). Per computed trial the program reports the untrusted observations sequences, normal_sequences, selfcheck_ok, abnormal_quotients, gcd_positive (about 2 of 5 centres) and max_quotient_degree. Supports H-NORMAL at m = 12 on the construction's own pairs; it says nothing about the scale m of the claim, the cost or the success probability.

experiments.scope: One trial of the algorithm at reduced depth, on the selected Orchard Poseidon target (proof.md 9.1, 9.5, 10.5.1). For a centre c from the trial seed the program builds F_2(c + X) (the F_N of proof.md 10.3, degree 25), its monic odd part g (degree m = 12), R = X^((p-1)/2) mod g and the complete Euclidean sequence of (g, R - 1) with its gcd G, exactly over F_p; deg G = k(c), the number of usable roots. If the sequence is normal and 1 <= k(c) <= 16, it isolates a root S of G (stage E, shifts from the seed), takes s = sqrt(S) and checks F_2(c + s) = F_2(c - s) by direct evaluation. Trials 0-255 are computed. A trial that passes returns two distinct canonical messages on the line whose digests agree on the first 6 bits (65 line points, certain by pigeonhole); any other trial returns two nulls. The checked pair count is the number of centres where one trial at depth 2 succeeds.
experiments.hypothesis: Every computed sequence is normal (H-NORMAL), and a trial returns a pair exactly when 1 <= k(c) <= 16 and its isolated root passes the check; at m = 12 the fraction of centres with 1 <= k(c) <= 16 is given by the law of proof.md 9.3, a theorem at this depth. The pair count is a reproducible observation consistent with that law; no probability, rate or population bound is drawn from it (public organizer seeds; nothing is assumed about the seeded trials being independent or identically distributed). Per computed trial the program reports the untrusted observations n_layers, m, gcd_degree, normal, abnormal_quotients, selfcheck, iso_rounds, root_check and witness_points. Supports the premises H-ONE and H-NORMAL at m = 12 on the construction's own polynomial; it says nothing about the scale m of the claim, where they are extrapolated.
